newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar firms above 113 yen in Tokyo on Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firms above 113 yen in Tokyo on Sakakibara.

text.p: *Dollar firms to above 113 yen by mid-morning Tokyo after MOF's Eisuke Sakakibara said there has been no change in the foreign exchange policy of the Ministry of Finance.
*Sakakibara, head of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, told Reuters: "The MOF's forex policy has not changed".
*"As with the U.S. Treasury, (the MOF) does not have any intention at all of using foreign exchange rates as an instrument of trade policy," Sakakibara added.
*Active short-covering led by interbank operators rapidly lifted dollar up against yen, as many sellers took wait-and-see attitude.
*Commercial buying ahead of local fixing also provided firm support.
*Dealers expect greenback to find support above 113 yen after Japanese official's comments on foreign exchange market.
*Dollar came off earlier lows due to short-covering and light purchases by Japanese importers, but topside capped at around 112.80 yen, dealers said.
*Dollar fell as low as around 112.30 yen in early Asian trade, but short-covering and commercial dollar buying took place after heavy falls on Monday.
*Traders cautious about selling dollar aggressively ahead of regular news briefing by Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka after cabinet meeting and Japan's current account data due out on Wednesday.
*There was talk that Japanese investors such as trust banks placed bids at lower end of 112-113 yen.
*"There were dollar purchases from operators who were expecting the dollar/yen to stay in a 112-115 yen range," said a senior dealer at a Japanese city bank.
*He said fall below 112 yen unlikely for today because of solid buying interest near 112 yen, although chance of drop towards 110 yen still possible in near term.
*"The market has not been satisfied with the dollar's fall," he said. But Japanese authorities could still be reluctant to see dollar fall below 110 yen," he added.
